afd.text:
000
FXUS62 KRAH 271115
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
615 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Gusty winds persist today, though below advisory criteria.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES... 
As of 138 AM Friday... 

1) Gusty winds and cool temperatures end our week before 60s return 
Saturday.

2) Turning warmer this weekend, followed by a period of showers 
Sunday evening and Sunday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 138 AM Friday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... Gusty winds and cool temperatures end our week 
before 60s return Saturday.

A vigorous upper-level trough presently across the southern 
Appalachians and lower OH valley will track through the Mid-Atlantic 
states today before exiting off Maine tonight. In its wake, quasi-
zonal flow takes over for Saturday. 

At the surface, an occluded low over the Lower Great Lakes will 
continue to bring gusty winds across central NC due to the continued 
tight pressure gradient and 35-40 kt winds in the lowest 5 kft. The 
winds are expected to be strongest into mid-morning, at which time 
surface winds of 30 to 35 mph will be common. This afternoon, it 
will remain gusty, though wind speeds aloft decrease to around 25-30 
kt, supportive of 25-30 mph wind gusts and infrequent 35 mph gusts. 
These wind gusts will finally start to relax tonight as the system 
pulls away and the gradient relaxes. Even still, gusts to 20 mph 
will still be around through the late evening. These gusts are shy 
of wind advisory criteria, although could still result in some minor 
downed tree limbs and blow around unsecured objects.

It will be a cool end to the week with low to middle 50s. Tonight, 
we drop down into the upper 30s to around 40, close to average for 
this time of year owing to the mixed boundary layer. Warmer weather 
is in store for Saturday with temperatures mainly near the lower 60s.


KEY MESSAGE 2... Turning warmer this weekend, followed by a period 
of showers Sunday evening and Sunday night.

Slightly above normal temperatures will return to central NC this 
weekend with deep SW flow ahead of the next mid-latitude cyclone 
that tracks NE from the Southern Plains NE into the MS Valley on 
Saturday night/Sunday, then into the OH Valley, Lower Great Lakes 
and Northern New England Sunday night/Monday. The associated 
northern-stream shortwave will quickly swing ENE across the TN/OH 
Valleys on Sunday evening then into the Mid-Atlantic on Sunday 
night, perhaps becoming negatively-tilted. Forecast highs are in the 
upper 50s to lower 60s on Saturday and lower to mid 60s on Sunday. 

Moderate to strong mid-level height falls will overspread central NC 
on Sunday evening/night as the aforementioned shortwave approaches, 
likely aiding in the development of a band of showers along and 
ahead of a cold front. Models continue to have good consensus on the 
strength and track of the low/shortwave, though the GFS is a bit 
slower compared to the ECMWF and CMC. PW values will briefly be 125-
175% of normal during this period, but rainfall amounts should not 
be too heavy due to a lack of instability and the progressive nature 
of the system. ECMWF/GFS/CMC ensemble means generally depict around 
a tenth to a third of an inch, highest NW and lowest SE, with 
deterministic guidance closer to a quarter to half an inch. A warm 
front will lift north through the area on Sunday evening, providing 
a brief window of dew points in the 50s before the cold front moves 
through. Low and mid level wind fields are certainly impressive with 
the GFS and ECMWF depicting a 50-60 kt jet streak at 925 mb and 90-
100 kts at 500 mb. Will need to watch the potential for any deeper 
convection bringing any of these winds to the surface, but 
confidence in this occurring is low given a lack of instability and 
poor low-level lapse rates. Even outside of any showers, S/SW wind 
gusts of 20-30 mph will be possible from Sunday afternoon into 
Sunday night.

Any rain chances will come to an end by early Monday morning. 
Temperatures should drop back to near normal on Monday and Tuesday 
as surface high pressure builds in from the TN and OH Valleys. 
Monday and Tuesday nights look chilly with good radiational cooling 
potential and forecast lows in the upper-20s to mid-30s.


&&

.AVIATION /12Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/... 
As of 615 AM Friday... 

A mixture of MVFR/VFR conditions are likely to start the TAF period. 
Ceilings have improved across the eastern sites, but MVFR ceilings 
will continue to be possible at all terminals into early afternoon. 
Guidance is mixed on the erosion of the MVFR ceilings, which leads 
to some uncertainty. Our latest forecast indicates most sites will 
lift to VFR by around 18z, though eastern sites may reach VFR sooner 
than anticipated. Regardless, southwest wind gusts will continue to 
be in place today, ranging from 25-30 kt into the afternoon, 
decreasing to around 15-20 kt tonight. Winds should finally relax 
after 03-06z.

Outlook: Low-level wind shear may develop early Sunday night ahead 
of a cold front and accompanying band of rain and MVFR to perhaps 
briefly IFR ceilings forecast to move across the forecast area later 
Sunday night-Monday morning. Nwly surface winds behind that front 
will be strong and gusty on Monday. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Kren/Danco
AVIATION...Kren
